title: Retention: bounded history of run evidence with an explicit prune action
outcome:
HOW
- Policy constants in src/test_runs.rs: keep the last N runs per root (N=20 proposed) plus any run referenced by an open review/tracker note (referenced runs are marked via a 'pinned' flag on the record; pinning is explicit).
- Prune candidates = terminal runs beyond N, not pinned, never running/unknown; computed on request, listed in the tab with sizes.
- POST /api/test-runs/prune {runIds} deletes only listed candidates after re-validation; UI button with confirm; never automatic.
- Ties to tm-uex8.9 (launcher evidence retention) and tm-gglr (marker-only directories: treat a run dir without results.json and without a live worker as unknown evidence, prunable only when explicitly listed).

DEPENDS ON: tm-ncc6.2, .7.

REVIEW FIXES (F12): DEPENDS ON tm-uex8.9 (the retention policy is decided there; this task implements the host-side prune only). Remove the tm-gglr tie (it concerns %TEMP% test roots, not review-runs). Never prune a dir whose results.json.pid is alive; deletions confined to the resolved review-runs path (no symlink following); prune never runs automatically (no timer, no boot hook).

OUTPUT TO FILE (Greg, 2026-09-23): HOST_LOG files under <review-runs>/host/ are pruned together with their run (same candidate rules); never while the pid is alive.
acceptance:
- Candidate computation excludes running, unknown, pinned and live-pid runs and keeps the newest N per root (unit test with a mixed fixture; N from tm-uex8.9).
- Prune deletes only listed candidate directories inside the resolved review-runs path; a symlinked entry is skipped; a second identical prune is a no-op.
- A boot with N+5 terminal run dirs deletes nothing and registers no timer (test).
